transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you for seeing me. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I just wanted to check in about some stress I've been having, if that's okay? 

I work as a construction supervisor, so the days get pretty long and hectic. Lately, I've noticed that sometimes when I get home after a really long day on site, or, you know, after a stressful neighborhood planning meeting... I end up eating a bit more than I probably should. Like, I'll just grab whatever is around—some leftover takeout, a bowl of cereal, maybe some chips. It's not a huge deal, I don't think, but sometimes I just eat until I feel, um, uncomfortably full. I just wanted to make sure that's normal, or, you know, get some advice on how to handle the stress better? Does that make sense?
Do you usually eat more when you're feeling stressed or upset?

Yeah, I think so. Um, mostly just when I'm stressed. Like I said, the job can be a lot sometimes, managing the crews and making sure everything is up to code... so when I get home, it's just a way to unwind, I guess? 

I don't think I do it when I'm, like, really upset or anything. Just... tired and needing a break. It's just a little bit of comfort eating, which I think a lot of people do, right? I mean, it's not like I'm eating everything in the house. Just a bit more than usual to help me relax. Is that... is that pretty common for people with stressful jobs?
Do you find yourself eating more when stressed even when you're not hungry?

Um, I mean, sometimes? I guess I don't always pay super close attention to whether my stomach is actually growling. 

It's more just... it's a habit, you know? You get home, you sit on the couch, you grab a snack. I think most people do that when they're trying to wind down, don't they? I wouldn't say I'm, like, stuffing myself when I'm completely full or anything bad like that. Just... having a little something because it feels nice after a long day. That's not too unusual, is it?
Do you usually feel guilty after eating more than you probably should?

Guilty? Um... no, not really guilty. I mean, maybe just a little bit annoyed with myself sometimes? Like, 'Oh, I probably didn't need that second bowl of cereal,' but... I don't beat myself up over it or anything. 

I think everyone feels a tiny bit of regret if they overdo it on a snack, right? It's just a normal reaction. I definitely don't let it ruin my night or anything like that. I just try to brush it off. That's the healthy way to handle it, isn't it? Just moving on?
Do you think you would still eat more when you get home if you didn't have stressful days at work?

Um, gosh, that's a good question. I'm... I'm really not sure, honestly. I haven't really thought about it like that. 

I guess if my job was super easy and I didn't have to worry about the crews and the deadlines all day, I might not feel the need to decompress quite as much? But... I mean, even on weekends or days off, it's just nice to relax and have a little treat, you know? I think most people still enjoy a good snack even when they aren't stressed out, right? 

So I'd probably still have a little something when I get home, just because it tastes good and it's a nice routine. It's just a normal part of enjoying the evening. Does that sound right to you? I try to keep it pretty balanced, mostly.
Do you think you would eat more when stressed if you hadn't learned to associate eating with relaxing at home?

Um, wow, that's... I don't know if I've ever really separated those two things in my head? 

I mean, eating and relaxing just sort of go together naturally, don't they? Like popcorn and a movie. I think if I didn't have that routine... maybe I'd find another way to unwind? Like taking a bath or reading a book? 

But honestly, I think it's just human nature to want something comforting when you've had a tough day. It's not really this deep, psychological thing where I've trained myself to need food to relax. It's just... nice. That's a pretty normal way to look at it, isn't it? I don't think it's anything to be concerned about.
Did you grow up in a household where eating was used as a way to cope with stress?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my family is pretty typical, I think. We definitely had family dinners and celebrated things with food, like birthdays and holidays, but... I don't remember anyone specifically eating just because they were stressed out. 

My parents were both pretty hardworking, so we were always just busy. If someone was stressed, they'd usually just go for a walk or maybe watch some TV to zone out. Food was just... food, you know? It was for meals and celebrations. 

I guess I've just picked up my little evening routine on my own. But it's not like a big coping mechanism or anything, just a nice way to end the day. That's pretty common, right? Most families are just normal about food like that, aren't they?
Has your eating habit after work ever interfered with your daily activities or relationships?

Um, no, not really! I mean, I'm definitely still showing up every day and doing my job, keeping the crews on track and everything. It hasn't affected my work at all, I promise. 

I guess... well, I have started turning down some of the after-work stuff lately? Like, if the guys want to grab a bite or a drink after a big meeting, I usually just say I need to head home. I just... I get a little anxious that the evening will get away from me if I stay out too late, and I really like having that quiet time to myself to unwind. 

But it's just because I'm tired from the day, you know? It's not a big deal to skip a few happy hours. That's pretty normal for someone with a demanding job, right? It's good to set boundaries and make sure I get enough rest, don't you think?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight or overall physical health since you started eating more in the evenings?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try to stay pretty active on the job sites anyway, so I think it balances out? 

I haven't really noticed any big changes in my weight or anything. My clothes still fit the same, and I feel fine physically. Maybe I feel a little sluggish sometimes the next morning if I stayed up too late, but nothing major. 

I try to make sure I'm drinking enough water and getting decent sleep, so I think my health is doing okay. It's totally normal for weight to fluctuate a tiny bit anyway, right? As long as I'm still feeling good and getting my work done, I don't think there's anything to worry about, is there?
Did something specific happen that made you start eating as a way to relax after work?

Um, no, not really. There wasn't like a big dramatic event or anything. 

I think it just sort of... started happening? Work got a little busier, and I was just coming home feeling a bit more drained than usual. You know how it is when you're managing a bunch of people all day—you just want a minute where nobody needs anything from you. So, sitting down with some food just felt like a quiet, easy way to switch off. 

It wasn't a conscious decision or anything triggered by a specific problem. Just a way to transition from work mode to home mode, I guess. That makes sense, doesn't it? A lot of people have little routines to help them decompress after a long day, right?
Do you think you would have developed this eating habit if you hadn't started using food as a way to relax after work?

Oh, um... I'm really not sure. I haven't ever thought about it like that, to be honest. 

I guess... maybe not? If I had just, I don't know, started going for a run after work or just reading a book to unwind instead, maybe I wouldn't have gotten into this routine. But it's hard to say for sure. I just kind of fell into it because it was easy and right there in the kitchen, you know? 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer! It's just hard to imagine how it would have played out otherwise. Do you think it usually happens like that for most people? Like, they just start doing something harmless to relax and it just becomes a habit? I hope I'm explaining myself okay.
Do you ever feel like your eating habit is causing you problems or distress?

Um, distress? No, I wouldn't say distress, really. I mean, I'm still showing up to work every day and doing my job just fine. My crew hasn't noticed anything, and the projects are all running smoothly. 

I guess... well, I have started turning down some of the after-work stuff. Like, if some of the guys want to grab a bite or a beer after a meeting, I usually make up an excuse and rush home. I just... I get a little worried that if I stay out, the evening will get away from me, and I won't have that time to just decompress in my own way. 

But that's not really a huge problem, is it? I mean, it's probably better for me to just go home and rest anyway instead of staying out late. Lots of people prefer to just go home after a long day, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing for my routine.
Do you think you learned to associate eating with relaxation from someone or somewhere else?

Um, I don't think so? I mean, I can't really think of anyone I learned it from. 

My parents weren't really like that. Growing up, food was just... food, you know? We ate dinner at the table, and that was about it. And the guys I work with, they mostly just unwind with a beer or watching the game. 

I think it really was just me figuring out what felt comforting at the end of the day. It's just so easy to grab something from the pantry when you walk in the door. I hope that's an okay answer? I'm trying to think if I read about it somewhere or saw it on TV, but honestly, it just kind of felt like my own little discovery. Is it pretty common for people to just start doing it on their own like that?
Did you ever notice anyone else in your life using food as a way to relax when you were growing up?

Oh, um, no... like I was just saying, I really didn't see anyone do that when I was younger. I'm sorry if I didn't explain that very well a minute ago! 

But yeah, my family was always pretty, I guess, normal about food. My parents didn't really snack or eat to wind down after a hard day. We just had our regular meals together at the table, and that was pretty much it. I never really noticed my friends' parents doing it either, to be honest. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a better example for you? I feel bad that I don't have a more helpful answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information... am I understanding your question right?
Do you ever feel bad about yourself after eating more than you probably should?

Um... feel bad? Well, I mean, I guess nobody really feels *great* if they've had a little too much, right? Like, say, on Thanksgiving or something. 

But... no, I wouldn't say I feel really bad about myself. Sometimes I might think, oh, I probably didn't need that last sleeve of cookies, but it's not a huge deal. I just kind of brush it off. I mean, I work pretty hard all day on the site, so I figure I'm burning a lot of it off anyway, you know? 

I just... I try not to let it get to me too much. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because it's really just a little overindulgence sometimes. That's pretty normal, isn't it?
Do you think your way of eating to relax is something you learned from your daily routine or if it's more of an instinctive response to stress?

Um... I guess I'm not totally sure? I mean, it doesn't really feel like an instinct, exactly. Like I said, I think it just kind of became part of my routine when I get home from the job site. 

It's just... you walk in, you're tired, the kitchen is right there, and it just sort of happens, you know? I wouldn't say I'm super stressed or anything, just... unwinding. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to give you a good answer, but I've never really thought about whether it's an instinct or a routine before. Do most people know the difference when they do it? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
Have you experienced any negative effects on your physical health that you think might be related to your eating habits?

Um... physical health? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I feel pretty healthy overall! 

I guess sometimes my throat gets a little scratchy, or my stomach might feel a bit unsettled, but honestly, working construction, there's so much dust and weird hours... I'm sure it's just from that. I try to drink a lot of water and take care of myself, so I haven't noticed anything bad happening. 

I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for... I just don't want to make a big deal out of normal little aches and pains. Is it okay that I haven't really had any physical problems from it? I just want to be honest with you.
Do you think your eating habit is interfering with your relationships or daily life in any significant way?

Um... interfering? No, no, I wouldn't say it's interfering in a big way. I mean, I'm still showing up every day, getting the job done, keeping the crews on schedule. Everything at work is totally fine! 

I guess... well, I have started saying no to some of the after-work stuff. Like, if the guys want to grab a bite after a long day, I usually just head home instead. I just... I get a little worried that if I stay out, the evening will just get away from me, and I won't have time to just relax and unwind the way I'm used to. 

But it's not a huge problem or anything! I mean, it's normal to just want to go home after work, right? I just hope I'm not making it sound like I'm isolating myself, because I still talk to everyone at work all day. Is that... does that sound like a normal thing to do? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Do you feel like your eating habit is causing you significant emotional distress?

Um... emotional distress? No, I wouldn't use a word like distress. I mean, I'm generally a pretty upbeat person! 

I guess sometimes I feel a little... maybe a bit guilty or just kind of frustrated with myself after I eat, but I think everyone feels that way sometimes when they overdo it, right? It's not like I'm sitting around crying about it or letting it ruin my day. I just kind of brush it off and focus on work the next morning. 

I really don't want you to think I'm some kind of emotional wreck or anything. I handle things pretty well, I think. Is it normal to just feel a tiny bit bad sometimes but still be okay overall? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
Do you feel like your eating habit is causing you significant emotional distress?

Oh, um... like I was just saying a second ago, no, not really. I'm sorry, did I not answer that right the first time? I can try to explain it better if you need me to! 

But yeah, I really wouldn't call it distress. I'm honestly fine most of the time. I just get a little annoyed with myself sometimes, but I always pull it together for work. I really try to stay positive and keep a good attitude for my crew. 

Is it okay that it doesn't bother me that much? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, so please let me know if I'm not making sense!
